mechanism_narrative: Sustained decline in RETAIL_REC over four consecutive weeks (-18.3 to -26.0) reflects a persistent downward trend in consumer mobility. This trend will continue over the next four weeks, producing further negative RETAIL_REC values relative to the baseline period.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC declined monotonically from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days exceeds the mean of the prior 28 days, or reverses to positive territory.

mechanism_narrative: Accelerating RETAIL_REC decline (from -18.3 to -26.0 over four weeks) combined with stable RESIDENTIAL elevation (+3.1 to +3.9) indicates a behavioral shift toward home-based activity. This substitution effect will suppress retail mobility further as consumers remain confined to residential spaces.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC falls more than 7 points week-on-week while RESIDENTIAL remains above +3
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL stable at +2.9 to +3.9 across all weeks
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL drops below +2 or RETAIL_REC stabilizes (week-on-week change less than 2 points) for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Persistent TRANSIT decline (-14.1 to -17.3) signals reduced commuting and public mobility access. Constrained transit access directly limits retail destination accessibility, suppressing RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -14 for four consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT consistently negative across all four weeks
failure_condition: TRANSIT recovers to above -10 and RETAIL_REC simultaneously increases by more than 5 points.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility collapsed from +10.9 to -24.6 over four weeks, indicating outdoor recreation restrictions. Consumers unable to access parks will redirect discretionary mobility toward retail venues, producing a compensatory increase in RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls below -20 for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS declined from +10.9 at t-3w to -24.6 at t-0w
failure_condition: PARKS remains below -15 and RETAIL_REC does not increase by at least 3 points over the next two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has stabilized around -12 to -17 across four weeks while RETAIL_REC continues to decline. This decoupling indicates that workplace restrictions alone do not explain retail decline; instead, retail-specific constraints dominate. RETAIL_REC will remain depressed independent of workplace recovery.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES stabilizes within a 5-point band while RETAIL_REC continues declining
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES range -12.7 to -17.0 while RETAIL_REC range -18.3 to -26.0
failure_condition: WORKPLACES rises above -10 and RETAIL_REC simultaneously increases by more than 4 points within two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility remains positive (+1.9 to +7.7) despite RETAIL_REC collapse, indicating essential retail access is maintained while discretionary retail is restricted. This policy-driven bifurcation will persist, keeping RETAIL_REC suppressed over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM remains positive while RETAIL_REC remains negative
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM positive across all weeks; RETAIL_REC negative across all weeks
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM and RETAIL_REC converge to within 5 points of each other, or both decline simultaneously by more than 10 points.

mechanism_narrative: The four-week observation window shows consistent negative RETAIL_REC and PARKS trends with stable RESIDENTIAL elevation, consistent with a seasonal or policy-driven lockdown regime. Absent external shock, this regime will persist, maintaining RETAIL_REC depression over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:All four weeks show consistent regime signature
failure_condition: Any of the three series reverses direction sharply (>8 points) within one week, or policy announcement signals imminent reopening.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT decline accelerated from -14.1 to -17.3 over four weeks while RETAIL_REC decline accelerated from -18.3 to -26.0. This parallel acceleration suggests a feedback loop: reduced transit access further constrains retail mobility, which in turn reduces transit demand. This negative spiral will continue over the next week.
candidate_trigger: Both TRANSIT and RETAIL_REC show week-on-week deterioration for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT declined 3.2 points from t-3w to t-0w; RETAIL_REC declined 7.7 points
failure_condition: Either TRANSIT or RETAIL_REC stabilizes or improves for two consecutive weeks while the other continues declining.
